messages.subject: Explanation of the word scale?
parts:
Not sure if any has asked this before, but I have always find it hard to understand why the word "scale" is used to represent the concept of aesthetic mapping of data. In Leland Wilkinson's Grammar of Graphics book, the explanation is that:
The word scale derives from the Latin scala, or ladder. The Latin meaning is
particularly apt for graphics. The visual representation of a scale —an axis
with ticks— looks like a ladder. Scales are the types of functions we use to
map varsets to dimensions.
But what does a ladder have to do with visual mappings? And what does " The visual representation of a scale —an axis with ticks— looks like a ladder." mean?

I hope that understanding this will help me better reason for how to make ggplot2 work. Thank you.

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Explanation of the word scale?
parts:
The explanation of scale in terms of axes is just an example. Conceptually a scale is simply a translation of a value to a visual representation. That visual representation can be positional (as in coordinates) or any other type (such as color intensity, size, height etc). In some of these cases it makes more sense to use a legend instead of scale, but conceptually it is the same.

In general just think of scales as the ways that makes it possible for you to mentally convert a plot to the data it represents
